what_happened: On a docs job (a glossary of project terms checked against BRIEF.md), the user corrected Athena's first reading. The reading required recording and testing every occurrence of a term name in BRIEF.md (criterion 4, plus the last negative test case in criterion 7). The user dropped this. "Athena" alone appears hundreds of times in BRIEF.md, so the check would be large and brittle. The user kept criteria 1-3, 5, 6 and 8 and the structural test's negative cases: missing sources field, non-existent source, dangling relation target, duplicate term.
cause: When Athena writes acceptance criteria, nothing makes it estimate how big or stable a check will be against the real source (here, how often a term appears in BRIEF.md). It adds criteria for completeness, as if more coverage were always better. The reading is also not sized or sanity-checked before the user sees it, so the user has to catch an infeasible criterion by hand.
prevention: Add a reading-review step before acceptance. For any criterion that quantifies over occurrences, such as "every", "all" or "each occurrence", it would count the matches in the named source files. If the count is over a set limit (for example 20), the step would flag the criterion and require a sampled or structural alternative, such as checking that each term has a defined source, instead of per-occurrence checking. The flag would show in the reading so the user sees it before approving.
proposed_request: Build the project glossary from BRIEF.md and its addenda, with these requirements. (1) Each term has a definition and a non-empty sources field naming real files. (2) Relations between terms point to terms that exist. (3) No term is duplicated. (4) Add a structural test with negative cases for a missing sources field, a non-existent source, a dangling relation target and a duplicate term. Do not record or test every occurrence of a term name in BRIEF.md, because "Athena" alone appears hundreds of times. Use the corrected term meanings already given: planning, job, Athena, Hermes and landed. Refer to Sri by name or as "they".
